coarse_skill_concept: Parse structured text log files (web access logs, profiler stack traces) using regex and awk/Python to extract and aggregate per-entity metrics.

task_judgments.reason: Each log line is one record with positional fields; awk field extraction and per-field aggregation (count, sort, uniq) directly solves every sub-task.

Aggregation by frequency is shared, but the core challenge is stateful multi-line block parsing to reconstruct traces and form composite 3-frame keys — a fundamentally different parsing model than single-line field extraction.

final_groups.skill_concept: Parse line-oriented structured log files using awk/bash positional field extraction to compute per-field aggregate statistics (counts, top-N, unique).
final_groups.reasoning: The entire solution reduces to awk field splits on fixed-format single-line records plus sort/uniq/wc aggregation — a single reusable line-oriented parsing and counting procedure.

final_groups.skill_concept: Parse multi-line block-structured trace logs with a state-machine reader, group blocks by composite top-N frame keys, and rank by frequency.
final_groups.reasoning: The dominant challenge is recognising trace boundaries, accumulating frames across lines into a tuple key, and then counting those tuples — none of which is addressed by the line-oriented awk pattern used in the other task.
